## Introduction

The Elimisha (Sponsorship) program main objective is to promote education among the under-privileged (orphaned or in strenuous economic conditions) children in Kibera community. The program aims to educate, empower and engage the children for a sustainable future.

## School Update

### Activities and Outputs

Kibera currently has 116 children in the program, 60 girls and 56 boys. 38 Children are in Primary School, 58 in High School, 7 in university doing a degree course, 9 in college doing a diploma course and 3 are yet to join colleges in January. We have 82 students in public schools and 34 in private schools.

#### University and College

-   7 Students are currently in university doing a degree course.

-   8 Students are currently in colleges doing diploma and certificate courses. One graduated in August (Certificate in Media). Three are yet to join as of January 2025. One student lost interest in what he was studying.

#### Parents update

One parent passed on due to cancer (Mama Fenny Aluoch).

#### Activities

-   School fee payment

-   Tuition classes

-   School and home visits

    -   Sixty-nine (69) families of the sponsored children were visited in the last six months.

-   Mentorship meetings

-   Picnic gatherings and hike

-   Hospital visits

-   Volunteering

Resources: Scholarships, finances, Spur Afrika staff and volunteers, teachers, mentors.

### Outcomes and Impact

-   More than 90% of the sponsored children attended school regularly.

    -   105 Students out of 112 students attended school throughout the school term. Four (4) students were absent due to sickness, three (3) students missed school due to indiscipline cases and unexplained absenteeism. Three are awaiting to join college in 2025.

-   Of the 112 students, 19 students’ performance was very excellent (Exceeded Expectation), 63 students were above average (Meeting Expectation), 15 students performed below average but were approaching the expectations (Approaching Expectation) and 14 students’ performance was very poor, below expectation (Below Expectation). One Student did not do the exams due to absenteeism from school.

-   Eleven form 4 students have successfully completed high school and are waiting for College or University placements in 2025.

-   One student has graduated from college, he was studying Film Production.

## Mentorship Update and School Holiday Programs

### Activities and Outputs

We had a Team building picnic with 112 children at Rowerlan scout’s grounds in August where the sponsored children had constructive play and learnt about the importance of Team work and strategy.

28 of Sponsored children attend an online career mentorship with Deloitte Australia; it was a great session of learning more about the various careers available in other countries as well as different departments that can exist within the same organization.

Seven group mentorship sessions were held. 112 students attended at least two sessions.

![Form 1 and Form 2 high school student group discussion on having a Mindset of possibilities](images/2024H2%20Elimisha%20Group.png){fig-align="center"}

Twenty (20) Sponsored children attend coding classes every Saturday afternoon for 2 hours for 5 months. Fifteen (15) children attended Chess classes. The crowning achievement of the chess class participants was being part of a regional competition in Nairobi, held in November. The Spur Afrika Team came in second place in the chess competition.

110 sponsored children and 15 facilitators attended Spur Afrika’s annual Camp held in November for 6 days. The theme was THRIVE and every day the students learnt from different sub-topics: mindset of possibilities, passions and interest, utilizing technology wisely, prioritizing our mental health and career preparedness. The children participated in team-building games, creative skits, candle-light dinner, talent show and had plenty of food! It was a great time for the Spur staff to get to learn and interact more with the sponsored children.

#### Resources and inputs

-   Spur Staff & Volunteers

-   Finances

-   Mentors

-   Counsellors

### Outcome and Impact

-   Improvement in level of self-expression

-   Improved school performance and attendance

![High school student group discussion during our annual camp. The theme of the camp was THRIVE.](images/2024H2%20Elimisha%20Camp%20Thrive.png){fig-align="center"}

## Health Update

### Activities and Outputs

-   From July to December, 11 children got sick and received medical attention from the hospital.

-   All children in the sponsorship program were taught how to properly brush their teeth and were given toothbrush and toothpaste.

#### Resources and inputs

-   2 Spur staff

-   NHIF (National Health Insurance Fund) and finances

-   Partnerships with doctors and hospitals

### Outcome and impact

-   Sponsored Children were able to access Better medical care, resulting in the decrease of absenteeism from school.
-   More children are brushing their teeth correctly leading to a decrease in dental problems.

## Challenges faced in the last six months

-   Some of the parents are still struggling to provide to their children school supplies and this may lead to the child being out of school. The tough economic times make it hard for the parents to prioritise their children’s needs. Approximately 35 parents are affected by this.
-   A few parents are irresponsible and do not take good care of their children or model positive behaviour
-   There were two indiscipline cases reported from children, one has seemingly lost interest in school as he is chronically absent from school with no explanation.
-   14 children recorded poor performances in their academics
-   Family misunderstandings between parents and their children.

## Budget update

-   Funds used so far in the last 6 months is **Ksh. 3,400,000** (approximately AUD 39,000).This includes cost of school fees paid in September, camp costs in November and salaries of workers in charge of the program.

![Hope Juma taking part in the games during our end of year camp with sponsored children](images/2024H2%20Elimisha%20Camp%20Hope%20Juma.png){fig-align="center"}

## Plans for next six months

-   Proposed spending in the next 6 months (2025) is Ksh. 3,600,000 (approximately AUD 41,000). This includes a salary for the workers who are in charge of the program, meetings, and other program related costs.

-   Due to the high cost of living and inflation, the cost of school fees still remains high compared to the previous years. There are also 11 students set to join college or universities, and the cost of this is also high.
